text:
alex wang: heads up, seeing sustained GPU memory growth on long-context workloads when serving the int8 quantized variant. looks like slots aren't being reclaimed after repeated long prompts, memory creeps until OOM on slow-batch traces.

maria g: can you paste the telemetry? is this on dedicated or hosted canary?

alex wang: hosted canary (eu-west), reproducer attached to the job. key lines from the trace:```kv_slots_total=1_024_000
evict_rate=0.002
slot_frag_pct=38.7
int8_recall_drop=0.9%
longctx_tail_length=65k_tokens```

perf-bot: alert: memory_growth_rate > baseline by 48% on canary-93 (model: rdx-13b-int8). stacktrace id: st-2467896543-1

jit patel: my first guess is hysteresis in the slot residency logic + quantized page packing. int8 compaction leaves small leftover fragments that the slab allocator can't reuse for new stripes, so effective free memory is lower than reported. under longctx we keep adding prefix entries so fragmentation accumulates.

sasha r: FWIW we ran the same workload on bf16 yesterday: memory growth ~6% over baseline but int8 had +52%. accuracy-wise bf16 kept logits stable, int8 had a ~1% token-level recall drop on the eval suite (small but consistent).

maria g: if it's fragmentation, we should confirm by forcing a compaction pass on the canary and see if mem drops. alex, can you add the compaction flag to the canary launcher? e.g. `--kv-compact-on-idle=1 --compact-threshold-pct=25` and rerun for 6hrs. also collect `slabmap_free_ranges` histogram.

alex wang: queued a canary with compaction flags. also instrumented kernel selection logs so we can see if runtime is switching to different GEMM kernels for short vs long sequences. link: https://perf.redwood/canary/2467896543

jit patel: another vector: our batching heuristics increase continuous batching window for int8 (to amortize kernel cost) which accidentally keeps KV pages hot longer -> prevents eviction. try reducing max_batch_delay for the canary to see batch/evict interplay.

sasha r: noted. quick experiment table we ran:
```
variant      | mem_growth | accuracy_delta
bf16         | +6%        | 0.0%
int8         | +52%       | -0.9%
int8+compact | +8%        | -0.9%
```
compact pass collapses a lot of fragments but accuracy stays unchanged for int8 (so compaction doesn't alter quant state, good).

maria g: if compaction fixes mem, we still need to decide tradeoff: compaction costs CPU/GPU pause and might add tail latency. alternative is smarter kernel selection: if seq_len > 16k and int8 recall drops above threshold, dynamically route those requests to bf16 kernel (or use hybrid caching where long prefixes stored bf16). this keeps int8 for short queries and avoids mem blowup on longctx.

jit patel: we can also tweak eviction hysteresis: make cold-to-hot promotion require N hits instead of immediate, shrink prefetch window for int8 batchers. both should reduce ghost pages.

alex wang: early canary results: compaction reduced fragmentation from 38.7% -> 6.2% and memory growth flattened. however tail p95 latency increased ~8ms during compaction windows.

sasha r: propose rollout plan: 1) enable `kv-compact-on-idle` in canary for 24h, 2) run int8 vs bf16 A/B on longctx-heavy routes and measure both mem & eval-regressions, 3) if compaction acceptable, add adaptive compaction that triggers only when frag_pct > 30% and evict_rate < 0.5%.

maria g: add additional metric: token-level BLEU/perplexity drift on the sentinel promptset and a 30-run sliding window for eval. we want to catch subtle regressions that don't show in single-run.

jit patel: I'll prototype eviction hysteresis change and a flag to route long sequences to bf16 kernels. I can put up a branch with toggles by EOD.

alex wang: assigning myself to run the compaction canary for 24h and gather slabmap histograms + per-kernel memory accounting. will post results here.

perf-bot: canary update: compaction-enabled canary stable at 3h, frag_pct=7.1%, mem_growth_rate down 46% vs previous baseline.

sasha r: perfect. after jit's branch we should run the hybrid kernel routing + smaller batch window experiments in parallel. try to keep canaries on same dataset so results are comparable.

alex wang: thanks. if we converge, follow-up PR should include a small telemetry flag in the console: `kv.fragmentation_pct`, `kv.compaction_runs`, and `kernel.route_fallback` to make ops decisions visible.

maria g: agreed. next sync tomorrow 10am to decide whether to promote compaction or go with kernel fallback.

alex wang: pinging owners: @jit patel (evict/hysteresis), @sasha r (canary+eval), @maria g (telemetry).

end of thread: plan = run compaction canary + prototype eviction toggles + parallel A/B for kernel routing.
